definitions.gloss: recent years; in recent years; lately
definitions.explanation: Refers to the past several years up to the present, used to introduce trends or changes that have emerged over a period of time.

examples.japanese: {近年|きんねん}、{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: In recent years, the number of tourists has been increasing.

examples.japanese: {近年|きんねん}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}{革新|かくしん}は{目覚|めざ}ましい。
examples.english: Technological innovation in recent years has been remarkable.

examples.japanese: {近年|きんねん}、{異常気象|いじょうきしょう}による{被害|ひがい}が{世界各地|せかいかくち}で{深刻|しんこく}になっている。
examples.english: In recent years, damage from extreme weather has become severe in various parts of the world.

notes:
Compound of {近|きん} (near, recent) + {年|ねん} (year). Typically refers to a span of roughly 5-10 years. More formal than {最近|さいきん}, which can mean "recently" on any timescale.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {近年|きんねん}の{傾向|けいこう} (recent trends)
- {近年|きんねん}まれに{見|み}る (rarely seen in recent years)
- {近年|きんねん}{急増|きゅうぞう}している (rapidly increasing in recent years)

USAGE:
Often appears at the beginning of sentences to set a temporal frame. Primarily a written or formal-speech word. In casual conversation, {最近|さいきん} or ここ{数年|すうねん} are preferred.
